title: Infosys Stock Drops 5% as Revenue Miss and Guidance Cut Trigger Fresh Analyst Downgrades
excerpt: India's second-largest IT firm missed quarterly revenue estimates, narrowed its FY27 growth forecast to 1.5%-3%, and named a CEO-designate — prompting brokerages to slash price targets to as low as $10.
body:
• Infosys Q1 FY27 revenue of ₹48,211 crore ($5.08 billion) and net profit of ₹7,769 crore both missed analyst estimates, sending U.S.-listed shares down 5%.
  • The company narrowed FY27 constant-currency revenue growth guidance to 1.5%-3.0% from 1.5%-3.5%, well below the Street's 2.5%-4.5% expectation.
  • TD Cowen, Susquehanna, and Stifel Nicolaus have cut price targets in recent weeks, with the lowest now at $10 — below the current ADR price of roughly $10.67.
  • Ashiss Kumar Dash, a 31-year company veteran, was named CEO-designate and will succeed Salil Parekh from April 2027.

Revenue Miss and Soft Volumes Rattle Investors

Infosys delivered a mixed Q1 FY27 on Wednesday, reporting revenue of ₹48,211 crore ($5.08 billion), a 14% year-on-year increase in rupee terms but a miss against the LSEG-compiled consensus estimate of ₹48,367 crore. In constant-currency terms, revenue grew 2.4% year-on-year and 1% sequentially — below the company's own expectations.

Consolidated net profit rose 12.2% to ₹7,769 crore, also short of the ₹7,832 crore analysts had penciled in. Earnings per share climbed roughly 15% year-on-year to ₹19.19.

CFO Jayesh Sanghrajka attributed the shortfall to a 50-basis-point revenue hit from a client program termination in the energy, utilities, resources and services (EURS) vertical and "volumes that were soft and weaker than expectations." Rivals Tata Consultancy Services and HCLTech, by contrast, beat their own quarterly estimates earlier this month, aided by strong financial services demand and a weaker rupee.

Guidance Trimmed Amid Macro Uncertainty

The bigger blow came from the guidance revision. Infosys narrowed its FY27 constant-currency revenue growth forecast to 1.5%-3.0%, shaving the upper end from the earlier 3.5%. Wall Street had expected 2.5%-4.5%.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=2S6tbyRxQPM

"Overall business environment continues to remain volatile. The low end of the guidance assumes further macroeconomic deterioration, while the high end assumes improvement — though less than what we had assumed in April."

— Jayesh Sanghrajka, CFO, Infosys

Sanghrajka said the revised outlook incorporates approximately 1.7 percentage points of contribution from the recently closed acquisitions of Optimum Healthcare and Stratus. He also flagged a shift toward offshore delivery that is expected to reduce revenue growth by 0.75 to 1 percentage point for the full year, and lower spending by a large European manufacturing client.

CEO Salil Parekh acknowledged that the stronger macroeconomic environment assumed in the earlier forecast's upper bound had not materialized, with clients remaining cautious on discretionary technology spending amid tariff uncertainty, geopolitical tensions, and inflation.

Brokerages Slash Targets

The results added fuel to a wave of analyst downgrades that had already been building. TD Cowen slashed its Infosys target to $10 from $13 on July 9, maintaining a hold rating — the most bearish call on the Street. Susquehanna followed on July 10, cutting its target to $12 from $14 with a neutral stance. Stifel Nicolaus lowered its target to $13 from $15 on July 16.

In June, JPMorgan trimmed its overweight target to $12.70 from $16.80, while Wells Fargo set an equal-weight target of $11. The consensus rating among tracked analysts now sits at "reduce," according to MarketBeat, with an average target of roughly $14 — a figure that itself may come under pressure after the guidance cut.

StoxBox analyst Sagar Shetty told Reuters the forecast downgrade "likely reflects a more pressuring environment going forward."

AI Growth and Large Deals Offer a Bright Spot

Not everything in the quarter was negative. AI-related services accounted for 8.2% of Infosys' revenue, up from 5.5% in the December quarter, and Parekh said AI revenue has been growing at a double-digit sequential rate for several quarters running. More than 80,000 Infosys employees now use coding tools such as Claude Code or Codex for client and internal work.

Large deal bookings totaled $3.6 billion across 22 contracts, with 61% representing net-new business. Three individual deals were valued at approximately $400 million each. The company also said 20% of large-deal total contract value came from vendor consolidation opportunities — a segment where Infosys sees itself as a net beneficiary.

Operating margin expanded 20 basis points sequentially to 21.1%, and free cash flow of $955 million equaled 116.5% of net profit. The balance sheet remains debt-free with $3.9 billion in cash.

CEO Succession Adds a New Variable

Infosys announced that Ashiss Kumar Dash, a three-decade company veteran who leads the EURS business, will take over as CEO and managing director from April 1, 2027, for a five-year term. Parekh, who led Infosys from $10 billion to $20 billion in revenue during his nearly decade-long tenure, will continue through March 31, 2027.

Dash is currently based in Los Angeles and will relocate to India in the coming months. A structured handover process will begin in October, with Parekh serving as mentor during the transition.

"Ashiss Kumar Dash is a safe, execution-focused appointment at a time when Infosys needs stability as much as transformation."

— Phil Fersht, CEO, HFS Research

What Diaspora Investors Should Watch

For NRI investors holding Infosys stock — either directly on the BSE/NSE or via the NYSE-listed ADR — the Q1 miss and guidance cut raise near-term risk. The ADR, which closed at $10.93 before the results, traded around $10.67 on Thursday, and several analyst targets now sit at or below current levels. With the consensus rating at "reduce" and the IT sector broadly under pressure from AI-driven spending shifts, the stock may need to demonstrate execution on AI monetization and deal closures before a re-rating.

Key catalysts to watch include the pace of AI revenue ramp through FY27, clarity on whether the macro environment improves enough to support the upper end of the new 1.5%-3% guidance band, and how smoothly the CEO transition proceeds. Infosys plans salary hikes from October, which will test whether margins can hold within the 20%-22% corridor.
nri_angle: NRI investors face near-term risk on Infosys ADR and domestic holdings as multiple brokerages cut targets below current prices amid guidance downgrade and AI-driven spending uncertainty.
